source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting company losses in a financial disclosure

1. Start with the accounting records.
2.
completion:
Prepare an Income Statement that is free of non-operating incomes,
and does not include capital gains. For example, if you receive dividends from shares in
IBM that you own, you can deduct the loss in value of those shares. But you cannot deduct the loss in value
of the shares in your own company.

It is not legal to use accounting records to disguise the real income or loss of a company. If you don't have the 
real income or loss in your records, do not proceed further.

3. Take the net loss shown on the Income Statement in #2 (line 2 + 3 + 4 + 5) and multiply by
4 months.

4. Take the amount from #3 and multiply by the fraction of time your company
is associated with the investment.
